articles.title: Amazon teams with Uber Eats for new Prime perks - Engadget
articles.text:
Amazon teams with Uber Eats for new Prime perks
Order on Amazon’s platforms and (sometimes) skip the delivery fees.
Amazon has a pretty long list of perks for members of its Prime subscription program, and today brings a new addition. The company now supports placing Uber Eats orders directly on its Amazon.com website and in the Amazon Shopping app in the US. The partnership with Uber will also grant $0 delivery fees to Prime Members on their Uber Eats orders of $25 or more placed via Amazon, as well as a promise of "Prime-exclusive offers available only on Amazon." No separate Uber account is needed to place the delivery orders and nearly 10,000 cities and towns in the US will support the integration.
According to the release from Amazon, the Uber Eats integration could save Prime users as much as $175 a year, although the exact amount will obviously vary depending on how much you rely on delivery for meals.
Amazon offered a year of free GrubHub+ access along with Prime starting in 2022. This subscription program, which includes $0 delivery fees and other perks tied to GrubHub orders, became a permanent benefit of Prime in 2024.

articles.title: Perplexity launches its own take on AI agents for work
articles.text:
Perplexity is taking on OpenAI and Anthropic with its own work-focused AI agents. The startup’s new always-on “Teammates” can take on multiple roles within a workspace, while pulling existing projects, skills, and memory from the Perplexity tools you already use.
Perplexity launches its own take on AI agents for work
Like OpenAI’s Dots and Claude Duet, Perplexity’s Teammates can perform an array of tasks while running 24/7.
Teammates integrate with Perplexity Computer, an AI system that can deploy agents on your device to complete tasks. But Perplexity says Teammates “build on top” of Computer by offering the ability to collaborate and complete “ongoing, large-scale work.” You can assign each Teammate different jobs that they can perform simultaneously — much like OpenAI’s Dots and Claude Duet. Perplexity’s take on the feature is much more expensive, however, as it requires a subscription to its $200 / month Max plan.
Perplexity notes that you can keep tabs on Teammates’ progress through individual threads in the Perplexity app, as well as interact with them in Slack. “Over time, we envision every org having hundreds of teammates working for each person,” Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas says on X.

articles.title: Zipline hits $21.5B valuation as Walmart expands bet on drone delivery | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Zipline has raised $1.5 billion and ramped up its partnership with Walmart, a pair of deals that have raised the autonomous drone delivery and logistics startup’s profile and valuation.
Zipline and Walmart reached a new multi-year agreement to add 300 drone delivery sites across the United States. The two companies have had a drone delivery agreement since 2021, but this deal is a significant jump from the 21 active drone delivery sites they have together today.
On the fundraising side, Zipline’s $1.5 billion raise was led by Paradigm, WCM Investment Management, and Layer Global, with participation from Valor Equity Partners, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Uber, Tiger Global, J.P. Morgan, ARK Invest, and Salesforce Ventures. Zipline is now valued at $21.5 billion.
The company, which has developed a drone delivery ecosystem that includes aircraft, launch and landing systems, and logistics software, said it plans to use the funds to expand its U.S. manufacturing facilities and hire more workers to build out a nationwide drone delivery network.
Founded in 2014, Zipline got its start in Africa, where it used its autonomous drones to deliver blood in Rwanda, and later expanded to Ghana and Nigeria. The California-based company began its first operations in the U.S. in 2020, ferrying medical equipment and supplies to Novant Health in North Carolina. The following year, it struck a deal with Walmart.
But it was in 2022 that Zipline’s business really started to take off in the United States. Zipline received its Part 135 air carrier certification from the Federal Aviation Administration that year, a critical regulatory hurdle that authorized the company to complete long-range commercial drone deliveries. It has locked in a number of partnerships since then, including with Uber earlier this year.
Zipline now uses its drones to deliver food, retail, agricultural, and health products in five African countries, several cities in the United States, and Japan. Zipline’s home delivery service uses Zipline’s Platform 2 drones, which are designed to carry up to eight pounds and travel to customers within a 10-mile radius. Its larger Platform 1 drones are used for long-range deliveries for enterprise, business, and government that can cover 120 miles round trip.
The company said Thursday that its share of delivery revenue grew from 10.8% to 34.9% between March and October of this year. This latest funding aims to push that metric even higher.

articles.title: Cục Thuế nghiêm cấm gây sức ép buộc người nộp thuế từ chối nhận tiền nộp thừa
articles.text:
Cục Thuế vừa có công văn gửi Thuế các tỉnh, thành phố, Chi cục Thuế Doanh nghiệp lớn và Chi cục Thuế Thương mại điện tử hướng dẫn việc xử lý hồ sơ chấm dứt hiệu lực mã số thuế.
Công văn được ban hành sau khi một số địa phương phản ánh vướng mắc trong quá trình xử lý hồ sơ chấm dứt hiệu lực mã số thuế và giải quyết nghĩa vụ thuế của người nộp thuế khi triển khai Chiến dịch Làm sạch mã số thuế - Tháo gỡ điểm nghẽn trong kinh doanh.
Theo hướng dẫn của Cục Thuế, đối với người nộp thuế đang ở trạng thái 06 (không hoạt động tại địa chỉ đã đăng ký), khi nộp hồ sơ đề nghị chấm dứt hiệu lực mã số thuế, cơ quan thuế quản lý trực tiếp có trách nhiệm cập nhật trạng thái mã số thuế của người nộp thuế và các đơn vị phụ thuộc trong thời hạn 1 ngày làm việc kể từ khi tiếp nhận đầy đủ hồ sơ.
Theo đó, mã số thuế được chuyển về trạng thái 06, lý do 03: "Người nộp thuế không hoạt động tại địa chỉ đã đăng ký và có hồ sơ chấm dứt hiệu lực mã số thuế" trên Hệ thống ứng dụng đăng ký thuế.
Cơ quan thuế không ban hành Thông báo mẫu số 17/TB-ĐKT về việc người nộp thuế ngừng hoạt động và đang làm thủ tục chấm dứt hiệu lực mã số thuế đối với trường hợp người nộp thuế đang ở trạng thái 06 và đã nộp hồ sơ đề nghị chấm dứt hiệu lực mã số thuế theo mẫu số 24-ĐKKT.
Về xử lý số tiền thuế nộp thừa khi người nộp thuế chấm dứt hiệu lực mã số thuế, Cục Thuế nêu rõ, cơ quan thuế có trách nhiệm hướng dẫn người nộp thuế hoàn thành nghĩa vụ thuế, thực hiện bù trừ nghĩa vụ thuế hoặc giải quyết thủ tục hoàn trả số tiền nộp thừa theo đúng quy định của pháp luật về quản lý thuế.
Việc xử lý không hoàn trả tiền nộp thừa và hoàn tiền nộp thừa được thực hiện theo Điều 43 và mục 2 Chương V Thông tư 89/2026 của Bộ Tài chính.
Tuy nhiên, Cục Thuế cho biết có tình trạng công chức thuế yêu cầu người nộp thuế làm văn bản từ chối nhận số tiền thuế nộp thừa để đóng hồ sơ, gây bức xúc trong dư luận.
Trước tình trạng này, Cục Thuế yêu cầu thuế các tỉnh, thành phố chỉ đạo các phòng, thuế cơ sở trên địa bàn và công chức thuế phụ trách hướng dẫn người nộp thuế lập hồ sơ nhận lại tiền hoàn thuế hoặc bù trừ nghĩa vụ thuế theo đúng trình tự, thủ tục pháp luật quy định.
Cục Thuế nghiêm cấm việc gợi ý, gây sức ép hoặc yêu cầu người nộp thuế từ chối nhận số tiền thuế được hoàn hoặc bù trừ nghĩa vụ.
Cơ quan này yêu cầu Thuế các tỉnh, thành phố và Ban Kiểm tra (Cục Thuế) tăng cường kiểm tra nội bộ, chủ động nắm bắt tình hình, thông tin phản ánh trên các phương tiện thông tin đại chúng để kịp thời xác minh và xử lý nghiêm nếu phát hiện vi phạm.

articles.title: Điện gió Savan 1 đạt doanh thu trên 1.200 tỷ đồng sau 9 tháng vận hành
articles.text:
“Quả ngọt” từ chiến lược đầu tư hạ tầng năng lượng xuyên biên giới
Theo báo cáo tài chính quý III/2026, lợi nhuận gộp lũy kế 9 tháng của dự án điện gió Savan 1 (giai đoạn 1) đạt gần 42 triệu USD (tương đương gần 1.100 tỷ đồng) với tỷ suất lợi nhuận gộp xấp xỉ 89%.
Kết quả kinh doanh của Savan 1 được tạo ra sau khoảng 16 tháng triển khai, từ hoàn thiện thủ tục, thi công nhà máy đến đầu tư hạ tầng truyền tải xuyên biên giới. Cùng với 48 tuabin, tuyến đường dây 220 kV dài gần 70km được xây dựng đồng thời, kết nối nguồn điện tại Savannakhet (Lào) với hệ thống điện Việt Nam qua khu vực Trạm biến áp Lao Bảo (tỉnh Quảng Trị).
Giai đoạn 1 của dự án điện gió Savan 1 có công suất 300 MW, cung cấp khoảng 0,9 tỷ kWh điện về Việt Nam mỗi năm. Giai đoạn 2 của dự án với quy mô công suất 195 MW dự kiến dự kiến được khởi công vào cuối năm nay. Savan 1 là dự án năng lượng đầu tiên của T&T Group tại Lào. Với việc hoàn thành 100% kế hoạch năm về doanh thu và lợi nhuận, Savan 1 đang tạo cơ sở vững chắc để T&T Group tiếp tục phát triển Savan 2 cũng tại tỉnh Savannakhet.
Tháng 10/2026, trong khuôn khổ chuyến thăm chính thức Lào của Thủ tướng Lê Minh Hưng và Đoàn đại biểu cấp cao Việt Nam, dưới sự chứng kiến của Thủ tướng Chính phủ hai nước, 17 giấy chứng nhận đầu tư và thỏa thuận hợp tác của doanh nghiệp đã được trao. Trong đó, dự án điện gió Savan 2 của T&T Group là một trong những hợp tác lớn nhất.
Dự án điện gió Savan 2 có công suất 495 MW, tổng mức đầu tư khoảng 768 triệu USD, dự kiến vận hành thương mại chậm nhất ngày 31/12/2028. Dự án này nằm trong kế hoạch hợp tác giữa Chính phủ Việt Nam và Chính phủ Lào năm 2026. Hai bên thống nhất tạo điều kiện để dự án triển khai xây dựng và vận hành thương mại phù hợp với pháp luật mỗi nước.
Theo T&T Group, khi Savan 1 và Savan 2 hoàn thành, tổng công suất của hai dự án dự kiến đạt 990 MW, hình thành cụm điện gió gần 1 GW. Đặc biệt, Savan 2 có thể tận dụng hệ thống truyền tải đã được hoàn thiện từ Savan 1, trong đó có tuyến đường dây gần 70 km kết nối nguồn điện tại Savannakhet với hệ thống điện Việt Nam. Việc hạ tầng truyền tải đã được hình thành giúp giảm bớt khối lượng phải triển khai mới, hỗ trợ quá trình kết nối và đưa Savan 2 vào vận hành phù hợp với tiến độ, kế hoạch đề ra.
Tầm nhìn chiến lược phát triển hạ tầng năng lượng
Là một trong những doanh nghiệp tư nhân đa ngành hàng đầu của Việt Nam, trong những năm qua T&T Group đã tập trung vào những lĩnh vực có vai trò nền tảng đối với tăng trưởng và phát triển bền vững của Việt Nam. Trong đó, năng lượng là một trong những lĩnh vực có tầm nhìn chiến lược của T&T, gắn với mục tiêu bảo đảm an ninh năng lượng, thúc đẩy tăng trưởng xanh và phát triển bền vững.
Từ năm 2013, T&T đã nghiên cứu và đầu tư vào các nguồn năng lượng sạch, hướng tới mục tiêu đến năm 2035 đạt 25-30 GW công suất, tương đương khoảng 10% tổng công suất nguồn của hệ thống điện Việt Nam.
Danh mục đầu tư của T&T Group trải rộng từ điện gió, điện mặt trời đến điện khí LNG, điện sinh khối, hệ thống lưu trữ năng lượng bằng pin (Battery Energy Storage System - BESS) và các nguồn năng lượng sạch khác như hydrogen xanh, amoniac xanh…
Cùng với sự phát triển của điện gió và điện mặt trời, điện khí LNG vì vậy cũng là một trong những hướng đầu tư được T&T Group quan tâm phát triển. Tại Quảng Trị, T&T Group cùng các đối tác Hàn Quốc tham gia đầu tư dự án điện khí LNG Hải Lăng giai đoạn 1 với công suất 1.500 MW.
Một dự án LNG đáng quan tâm khác mà T&T Group đang xúc tiến các thủ tục đầu tư là dự án điện khí LNG Long Sơn công suất 1.500 MW tại TP.HCM. Tháng 9/2026, T&T Energy (đơn vị thành viên của T&T Group) và TotalEnergies Gas & Power Activities đã trao thỏa thuận hợp tác nghiên cứu cơ hội phát triển dự án.
Bên cạnh phát triển các nguồn điện, một hệ thống năng lượng có khả năng đáp ứng nhu cầu tăng trưởng cao còn cần sự kết hợp giữa hạ tầng truyền tải, công nghệ lưu trữ và các giải pháp điều tiết. Trong đó, hệ thống BESS đóng vai trò hỗ trợ cân bằng cung - cầu, đặc biệt khi tỷ trọng điện gió và điện mặt trời ngày càng tăng. Công nghệ này cho phép lưu trữ điện khi nguồn cung dồi dào và cung cấp trở lại hệ thống khi cần thiết. Với tầm nhìn chiến lược, T&T Group hiện cũng đang mở rộng hợp tác với các đối tác công nghệ quốc tế trong lĩnh vực BESS và chuyển đổi số trong năng lượng, hướng tới nâng cao hiệu quả khai thác nguồn năng lượng tái tạo.
(Nguồn: T&T Group)

articles.title: Salon is shutting down after 31 years
articles.text:
Salon launched 31 years ago as one of the first online-only news magazine outlets, and it announced today in an unsigned post that it’s ceasing publication.
Salon is shutting down after 31 years
Salon says its publishing model is ‘no longer sustainable.’
The company said that the “business realities of independent digital journalism have changed profoundly over the years,” and it decided that its publishing model is “no longer sustainable.” It didn’t go into detail about why, but many websites are grappling with “Google Zero” and the impact of AI tools. When reached for comment, Salon general manager Amanda Wolfe pointed The Verge to today’s announcement post.
“Thirty-one years is a remarkable run, but what matters most is what happened during those years: the journalism, the ideas, the voices, the conversations and the community that grew around them,” Salon said in its post. “Salon helped demonstrate what digital journalism could be and could become. We hope that legacy will continue to matter long after today.”
On Bluesky, Salon chief content officer Erin Keane says that the editorial archive will “stay live for now.”
Current Salon owner Find.co acquired Salon in 2023 and describes itself as a “Performance Marketing Ecosystem transforming crypto marketing with performance and precision.”

articles.title: SoundCloud lets ElevenMusic users publish AI-made songs directly
articles.text:
SoundCloud is opening a direct publishing route for music made with the ElevenMusic app, the AI music generation platform from ElevenLabs, allowing creators to send AI-generated tracks to the streaming platform without exporting and uploading them manually.
Previously, users had to download their tracks from ElevenMusic before uploading them to SoundCloud themselves. With the new integration, SoundCloud becomes the first platform outside ElevenMusic where users can publish their creations directly.
Tracks uploaded through the integration will carry a label identifying ElevenMusic as their source, making the use of AI visible to listeners. SoundCloud also prohibits AI-generated content that misleads audiences about its origins or creators, including music that impersonates other artists.
The partnership comes with a subscription offer for musicians. SoundCloud Artist Pro subscribers will receive three months of ElevenMusic Pro at no cost. The plan normally costs $9.99 a month and includes the ability to generate up to 1,000 songs monthly, as well as tools for separating tracks into individual elements such as vocals and drums.
“SoundCloud has always been a place where artists experiment, push boundaries, and turn creative ideas into something bigger,” said Eliah Seton, CEO of SoundCloud.
ElevenLabs, best known for its AI voice technology, entered the music market in 2025 with its first music generation model. In April, it launched ElevenMusic as a standalone app, allowing users to create songs from lyrics, melodies, or moods, as well as remix tracks by other artists.
“We built ElevenMusic to help more artists create, experiment and reach their fans,” said Mati Staniszewski, CEO and cofounder of ElevenLabs. “Music creation and discovery belong together and now, with SoundCloud, that music can reach even more audiences and communities.”
For SoundCloud, the agreement is part of a broader effort to bring AI tools into its platform. Last month, it partnered with Moises, an app used to edit existing music, and it already has an agreement with Google’s Flow Music.

articles.title: TikTok quietly launches a stand-alone TikTok Shop app | TechCrunch
articles.text:
TikTok has quietly launched a stand-alone TikTok Shop app in select markets as it continues to expand its e-commerce ambitions. The app will offer personalized product recommendations, the ability to shop through livestreams and short-form videos, app-exclusive deals, in-app checkout, order tracking, and customer support.
The app, which was first spotted by social media consultant Matt Navarra, is available in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and the Philippines on iOS and Android.
The launch of a stand-alone app gives TikTok Shop a chance to reach shoppers beyond the main TikTok platform and compete more directly with established e-commerce apps like Amazon and Temu. It also suggests that TikTok is prepared to invest more heavily in social commerce by giving Shop its own dedicated destination rather than simply keeping it within the main app.
TikTok did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment regarding the rollout.
It’s unknown whether TikTok plans to release the app more widely and bring it to the United States. If TikTok does bring the app to the U.S., it would be competing not only with Amazon and Temu but also with big-box retailers like Walmart and Target, whose customers have grown accustomed to routinely ordering through the stores’ apps.
According to the app’s description, users will be able to access free shipping offers and exclusive first-order benefits, along with “secure payments for safe checkout.” By offering users app-exclusive deals, the company is incentivizing them to shop in the app rather than the main TikTok app.
Interestingly, the launch creates something of a full-circle moment in the rivalry between TikTok and Amazon. While Amazon previously introduced a TikTok-like short-form video feed called Inspire to draw consumers’ attention away from apps like TikTok and drive sales on its platform instead, TikTok is now making a similar play in reverse. With its new stand-alone commerce app, TikTok is looking to draw consumers away from platforms like Amazon and fuel more purchases within its own ecosystem.
The launch marks another step in TikTok’s efforts to branch out beyond social media. Although the company was once primarily focused on social networking and entertainment, TikTok has gradually ventured into new areas.
Beyond TikTok Shop, the company has added games, restaurant guides, sports hubs, hotel booking, and microdramas, and is also exploring payments.

articles.title: The midterms proved once and for all that X is not real life
articles.text:
A week before the midterm elections, Vice President JD Vance hosted a town hall in Texas with Fox News host Jesse Watters. It was a friendly event with a friendly audience in what should have been a friendly state, and maybe that’s why Vance couldn’t help himself. When a college student earnestly asked how the right expected young people like her to settle down and have kids, given the ever-growing cost of living, Vance replied with a quip about Jon Husted’s ass.
The midterms proved once and for all that X is not real life
The student, Kate White, introduced herself as the vice president of the Texas Christian University chapter of Turning Point USA, the conservative group started by Donald Trump ally Charlie Kirk. She was offering Vance an opportunity to explain how MAGA could work for young people, and he turned it into a joke. Vance did eventually answer the question, saying Republicans don’t pay enough attention to the issue of affordability and blaming rising housing costs on institutional investors and the “20 million illegal aliens” supposedly living in the United States. But the order of operations revealed the fatal flaw of Republicans’ 2026 strategy: Everything is a gag to them, and they’re way too online.
For the past decade, Republicans have adhered to Steve Bannon’s maxim that politics is downstream from culture. This fixation with liberals’ alleged capture of elite institutions has animated the right’s war against Big Tech and in particular social media platforms — which the right claims actively silenced conservative voices — and its crusade against diversity, equity, and inclusion. With his purchase of X, Elon Musk finally succeeded in building a conservative platform where right-wing voices not only had real influence but also a direct line to those in power. More recently, some people have claimed that Musk’s X is the only social media that really represents the people, unlike platforms like Bluesky, which have more left-leaning user bases.
Cocooned in their online echo chamber, MAGA figureheads convinced themselves the public was on their side, even when polling suggested otherwise. They ignored their base’s valid concerns about affordability and served them nonsensical memes instead. And they failed spectacularly in the realm where it actually mattered: politics. X, we can now declare once and for all, is not real life. Republicans not only lost historically red states like Texas, Kansas, and South Carolina, but barely managed to win Florida. The Senate race in Mississippi, of all places, is still too close to call.
Vance, especially, is a creature of X, where his following list includes such illustrious accounts as Raw Egg Nationalist, Bronze Age Pervert, Howling Mutant, and Captive Dreamer. But White House aides, department employees, and Hill staffers are stewing in the same ecosystem. Writer John Ganz has termed this phenomenon “groyperfication,” after followers of influencer Nick Fuentes, who call themselves groypers. This is a useful shorthand, though Fuentes’ fans are mostly too NEET-pilled to land jobs on the Hill. American Moment, a boot camp for young conservative up-and-comers, reportedly screens out groypers. There’s a real need for such protective measures. Kingsley Wilson, the hard-right press secretary for the Department of War (or per its legal name, Defense), has posted antisemitic conspiracy theories about Leo Frank, a Jewish man who was lynched in Georgia 1915 for allegedly raping a teenage girl. (Historians largely believe Frank was innocent.) The Department of Homeland Security regularly posts fascist fancams and wink-wink references to white supremacist memes.
Republicans saw their 2024 victory as a mandate. Having clawed the White House and Congress back from Democrats, they assumed the public was on board with MAGA’s cultural project when in fact people were largely mad about the price of eggs. And with two years of dominance under their belt, they decided to go even harder on culture, not realizing — or maybe just not caring — that people are still mad about gas prices and groceries.
Cocooned in their online echo chamber, MAGA figureheads convinced themselves the public was on their side, even when polling suggested otherwise.
In the run-up to the midterms, the Department of Education was posting about “Malfoid” — a gender-swapped version of Draco Malfoy from Harry Potter that far-right influencers claimed would save Western literature from the scourge of wokeness. The Department of Homeland Security was bragging about record lows in legal immigration, which outside white nationalist circles is typically not considered a negative thing. Pseudonymous shitposters like Howling Mutant were posting memes comparing themselves to noted child murderer Anakin Skywalker, the new avatar for the online right. Musk, a Republican megadonor, got in on the fun, as did Katie Miller, wife of ultranationalist White House adviser Stephen Miller, who dressed up as Anakin’s wife Padmé Amidala for Halloween. (Katie Miller’s last government role was advising Elon Musk’s failed Department of Government Efficiency; now she devotes her time to throwing lavish parties and hosting a podcast no one listens to.)
Most of the American public isn’t on X, but the conversations conservatives have there do bleed out into the mainstream — often with disastrous results. Bo French, the Republican candidate for Texas railroad commissioner, lost his election by a huge margin after posting anti-Indian memes on X. (Asian American voters, including Indian Americans, moved to the left in Texas elections down the ballot.) Musk did his part to drive turnout, spending nearly half a billion dollars on Republican candidates and PACs. But even Musk’s money failed to make up for voters’ dissatisfaction with Republicans’ performance, perhaps because the ads he funded focused largely on culture war issues that were out of step with voters’ concerns about the cost of living.
And Miller, it turns out, didn’t even vote, telling CBS Newsshe feared doing so would put her safety at risk, since Virginia law makes voters’ home addresses public. (The Millers, like other members of the Trump administration, live on a military installation with tight security; it’s unlikely intruders would be able to get to their home.) Republican myopia may have contributed to their poor performance across the board, including with groups that were touted as their new base. One poll found that a majority of young men of all races — including young white men — voted for Democrats in the midterms.
In a long postmortem on X — reportedly posted without input or permission from White House officials — Vance said he asked “the smartest data guy” he knows for insight on the electorate ahead of the midterms. Vance claims several pollsters told him that voters’ main concerns were the war against Iran, the cost of living, and America’s relationship to Israel. So why didn’t Republicans listen?
The answer lies in the algorithmic nature of social media, X especially. If you interact with even one post about a relatively niche topic — say, genderbent Harry Potter fanfiction — the algorithm will feed you post after post after post about the same thing. Just like Trump spent the early years of his first term obsessing over Fox News, the single mainstream network that would reflect his biases back to him, MAGA is now all in on X. And if you’re the kind of person who spends a lot of time scrolling, you may even delude yourself into thinking the issue clogging up your feed is something people just can’t stop talking about.

articles.title: Nuôi chồn hương sau lần chọn nhầm giống, ông chủ Nghệ An thu gần 2 tỷ/năm
articles.text:
Trước khi bén duyên với nghề nuôi chồn hương, anh Trần Mạnh Hùng (40 tuổi, trú tại khối Hưng Hòa 3, phường Trường Vinh, Nghệ An) có 10 năm đi xuất khẩu lao động tại Hàn Quốc. Trong thời gian này, anh ấp ủ ý định phát triển mô hình nuôi động vật hoang dã, từng tìm hiểu về dúi và lợn rừng.
Năm 2018, sau khi trở về nước, anh dành thời gian khảo sát thị trường và nhận thấy nhu cầu đối với những vật nuôi trên đã dần bão hòa.
Trong thời gian làm nghề xây dựng, qua những lần tiếp xúc với khách nước ngoài và thưởng thức thịt chồn hương, anh đặc biệt ấn tượng với hương vị của loại đặc sản này.
Qua tìm hiểu tại các nhà hàng, anh nhận thấy chồn hương được nhiều cơ sở kinh doanh tìm mua, trong khi nguồn cung chưa đáp ứng ổn định nhu cầu thị trường.
Nhận thấy cơ hội phát triển, anh Hùng bắt đầu tìm hiểu kỹ thuật nuôi trên mạng, đồng thời trực tiếp đến tham quan một số trang trại ở TPHCM và các tỉnh miền Tây. Sau quá trình tìm hiểu, anh quyết định đầu tư 200 triệu đồng xây dựng chuồng trại, mua 14 con chồn giống về nuôi.
Do chồn hương là động vật hoang dã thuộc diện quản lý, anh Hùng cho biết đã thực hiện các thủ tục đăng ký cơ sở nuôi và hoàn thiện hồ sơ theo hướng dẫn của cơ quan kiểm lâm trước khi triển khai mô hình.
Thế nhưng, khởi đầu không thuận lợi như kỳ vọng. Sau khoảng một năm, đàn chồn phát triển, bắt đầu sinh sản nhưng liên tục xuất hiện tình trạng ăn con non.
“Bài học đắt giá nhất khi khởi nghiệp là tôi không tìm hiểu kỹ nguồn gốc con giống. Sau này, khi tìm hiểu sâu hơn mới biết giống mua về không đạt chuẩn”, anh Hùng nhớ lại.
Hơn một năm bỏ công chăm sóc, đầu tư thức ăn và chuồng trại, cuối cùng anh phải bán toàn bộ 14 con giống với giá chồn thương phẩm. Cuối năm 2019, khu chuồng nuôi từng được kỳ vọng trở thành sinh kế mới của gia đình rơi vào cảnh bỏ trống.
Vượt thất bại, gây dựng trang trại chồn hương tiền tỷ
Không từ bỏ ý định, anh Hùng tiếp tục dành thời gian nghiên cứu tập tính của chồn hương, cách phối giống, chăm sóc, phòng bệnh và lựa chọn thức ăn. Đặc biệt, anh chú trọng tìm hiểu thị trường, nguồn cung và đầu ra trước khi quyết định tái đàn.
Tháng 8/2022, sau khi tích lũy thêm kinh nghiệm, anh vào tận Tiền Giang để lựa chọn từng con giống. Lần này, anh mua 58 con, trọng lượng mỗi con khoảng 1,7-1,8kg, với mong muốn xây dựng đàn nuôi có chất lượng tốt, ổn định lâu dài.
Rút kinh nghiệm từ lần đầu thất bại, anh Hùng thay đổi vật liệu làm chuồng, chuyển từ sắt sang inox để hạn chế gỉ sét, thuận tiện vệ sinh và tăng độ bền trong quá trình sử dụng. Mỗi ô chuồng có diện tích đáy khoảng 0,8m2.
Thức ăn cho chồn chủ yếu gồm cá rô phi, đầu gà, chuối, trứng gà lộn và vịt lộn.
“Chồn hương thường được cho ăn vào cuối buổi chiều. Bình quân, một con trưởng thành tiêu tốn khoảng 1.800-2.000 đồng tiền thức ăn mỗi ngày. Sau khoảng 13-18 tháng nuôi, chồn có thể đạt trọng lượng 3-4 kg/con”, anh Hùng chia sẻ.
Cùng với chế độ dinh dưỡng, anh đặc biệt chú trọng vệ sinh và phòng bệnh. Mỗi sáng, chuồng trại được xịt rửa sạch sẽ, chất thải dẫn xuống hệ thống hố tự hoại bên dưới. Định kỳ mỗi tuần, anh phun thuốc sát khuẩn để hạn chế mầm bệnh, nhất là khi thời tiết thay đổi.
Theo anh Hùng, chồn hương không đòi hỏi quá nhiều thời gian chăm sóc nhưng người nuôi phải thường xuyên theo dõi tập tính, sức khỏe và khả năng sinh sản của đàn. Mỗi ngày, anh dành khoảng 2 giờ vệ sinh chuồng trại, cho ăn; thời gian còn lại chủ yếu để quan sát, kiểm tra từng con.
Từ 58 con giống ban đầu vào tháng 8/2022, sau gần 3 năm gây dựng và nhân rộng, đến nay trang trại có khoảng 500 con trên diện tích hơn 400m2.
Nhiều nhà hàng ở các tỉnh phía Bắc liên hệ đặt mua nhưng trang trại chưa thể cung cấp thường xuyên với số lượng lớn. Hiện anh chủ yếu bán chồn cho các nhà hàng tại Nghệ An và Thanh Hóa.
Chồn thương phẩm tại trang trại hiện có giá 1,5-1,8 triệu đồng/kg; chồn giống được bán với giá 9-11 triệu đồng/cặp. Năm 2025, gia đình anh Hùng thu về hơn 1,9 tỷ đồng. Sau khi trừ các khoản chi phí thức ăn, điện, nước và một số chi phí khác, anh đút túi hơn 1 tỷ đồng.
Có đầu ra tương đối ổn định, anh Hùng không muốn chỉ phát triển trang trại theo hướng tự nuôi và mở rộng số lượng đàn. Thay vào đó, anh đang tính toán xây dựng mô hình chăn nuôi vệ tinh, phối hợp với Hội Nông dân phường hỗ trợ người dân về con giống, kỹ thuật và kết nối tiêu thụ sản phẩm.
Ông Trần Xuân Hải, Chủ tịch Hội Nông dân phường Trường Vinh, cho biết trên địa bàn hiện có 4 hộ nuôi chồn hương, trong đó trang trại của anh Trần Mạnh Hùng thuộc nhóm có quy mô lớn. Nhờ chủ động nghiên cứu, tìm tòi và tích lũy kinh nghiệm, mô hình chăn nuôi của anh Hùng mang lại hiệu quả kinh tế cao.
Theo ông Hải, Hội Nông dân phường vừa tổ chức tập huấn, hướng dẫn kỹ thuật nuôi chồn hương. Một số hội viên cũng đang chuẩn bị xây dựng chuồng trại, hướng tới liên kết phát triển và nhân rộng mô hình trên địa bàn.

articles.title: Blue Origin delays New Glenn's return to flight until January
articles.text:
Blue Origin has pushed New Glenn’s return to flight to January 2027, CEO Dave Limp told staff, Bloomberg reports. The rocket has been grounded since it exploded on its only launch pad in May, delaying Amazon Leo satellites and NASA’s Moon plans.
Blue Origin has pushed back the return of its New Glenn rocket to January, chief executive Dave Limp told staff on Wednesday, Bloomberg reported. The company had pledged to fly again before the end of 2026, after the rocket exploded on its pad in May.
“This small adjustment doesn’t diminish what we’ve accomplished or the importance of the work still ahead,” Limp wrote in a memo seen by Bloomberg. “Returning New Glenn to flight remains our top priority.”
The Financial Times first reported the delay. Blue Origin declined to comment.
New Glenn blew up during an engine test on 28 May, destroying the rocket and badly damaging Blue Origin’s only New Glenn pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida. The company has spent six months rebuilding it, and Limp said bad summer weather slowed the work. In June, Blue Origin said it had not found the cause yet.
The delay hurts Amazon, Jeff Bezos’ other company. New Glenn was due to carry 48 Amazon Leo internet satellites on its next flight, and the FCC has already cut Amazon’s spectrum priority for satellites launched late.
It also matters for NASA. New Glenn is meant to launch Blue Origin’s Blue Moon lander, which NASA plans to use to land astronauts on the Moon under its Artemis programme.
The rocket is years behind schedule and has flown only three times since January 2025, leaving SpaceX far ahead. In July, Blue Origin was reported to be taking outside money for the first time, at a $130B valuation.

articles.title: Dropbox acquires Tigris Data for $350M to bolster its AI infrastructure | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Dropbox is making a big push into AI infrastructure with a $350 million acquisition of cloud technology company Tigris Data, marking what appears to be its largest acquisition to date.
Announced Thursday, the deal is expected to strengthen Dropbox’s AI infrastructure capabilities and support the development of DBX Agent Cloud, a new storage platform aimed at businesses and developers building AI models and agents.
Dropbox told TechCrunch via email that the transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026. The company also said it currently has no plans to reduce headcount as part of the acquisition. The company already cut 9% of its global workforce last month, WSJ reported.
DBX Agent Cloud will initially offer object storage as a stand-alone product, allowing businesses to purchase storage independently and use it with existing tools and applications built for Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service), which is a cloud storage service that enables businesses to store and retrieve large volumes of data.
Beyond its infrastructure ambitions, Dropbox is also bringing more AI capabilities to its core product. Users will be able to ask AI to perform supported tasks using their files, choose between different AI models, and connect their Dropbox content to third-party tools, including ChatGPT, Claude, and Muse.
The company also plans to expand DBX Agent Cloud with additional capabilities designed to help AI systems work with different types of content, including documents, images, audio, and video. Other planned additions include filesystem features that will allow AI agents to manage files and maintain continuity across tasks and sessions.
Dropbox says the updated experience has already reached more than 70,000 teams. The initial rollout is available to eligible Standard and Advanced customers in the U.S., U.K., and Australia, with broader availability planned for 2027.
Tigris Data was founded by former Uber engineers who helped develop the ride-hailing company’s storage infrastructure. The company provides cloud storage technology that helps businesses store and access data across different regions. Its platform automatically positions data closer to the users and computing resources that need it, helping reduce access times and improve performance.
Tigris Data raised $25 million in a Series A funding round last year.
While the Tigris deal appears to be Dropbox’s largest acquisition, it is not the company’s first move to expand its AI capabilities through M&A. Dropbox has previously acquired several AI-focused companies, including Reclaim.ai, Promoted.ai, and Mobius Labs.

articles.title: Blue Origin’s next launch now won’t happen until 2027
articles.text:
Blue Origin plans to do its next New Glenn rocket launch in January 2027, according to CNBC and the Financial Times, which cite a memo from CEO Dave Limp sent to staff. The new timeline follows a May launchpad explosion that damaged Blue Origin’s New Glenn launchpad ahead of a flight that would have brought Amazon Leo satellites into space.
Blue Origin’s next launch now won’t happen until 2027
Blue Origin had been aiming for a launch at the end of this year after a launchpad explosion in May, but now it’s reportedly targeting January.
In October, Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos told Fox News that the company was aiming for a December New Glenn launch, joking that it could be “probably December 31st.” The new, revised launch window is “about 10 days later than Blue Origin’s earlier launch target,” CNBC reports. Limp also reportedly cited bad weather as having an effect on the launchpad rebuilding process.
“This small adjustment doesn’t diminish what we’ve accomplished or the importance of the work still ahead,” Limp wrote in his memo, per CNBC and the FT. “Returning New Glenn to flight remains our top priority — it’s worth it.”

articles.title: Giá điện kinh doanh giờ cao điểm đắt gấp 2 - 3 lần giờ thấp điểm
articles.text:
Tập đoàn Điện lực Việt Nam (EVN) cho biết, giá bán lẻ điện bình quân được điều chỉnh giảm 2% từ ngày 1/11/2026, xuống còn gần 2.160 đồng/kWh, chưa bao gồm thuế giá trị gia tăng (VAT).
Ngày 4/11, EVN công bố biểu giá điện mới theo Quyết định 2892/QĐ-BCT do Bộ Công Thương ban hành ngày 31/10/2026. Quyết định này quy định giá bán điện áp dụng cho từng nhóm khách hàng, trong đó có nhóm sản xuất, kinh doanh và sạc xe điện.
Theo biểu mới, giá bán lẻ điện cho nhóm khách hàng kinh doanh khác được chia thành hai cấp điện áp, gồm từ trung áp trở lên (trên 1 kV) và hạ áp (đến 1 kV). Mỗi cấp điện áp áp dụng 3 mức giá tương ứng với khung giờ bình thường, thấp điểm và cao điểm.
Cụ thể, ở cấp điện áp từ trung áp trở lên, giá điện giờ bình thường là 2.829 đồng/kWh, giờ thấp điểm 1.577 đồng/kWh và giờ cao điểm 4.924 đồng/kWh.
Đối với cấp điện áp hạ áp đến 1 kV, giá điện giờ bình thường là 3.089 đồng/kWh, giờ thấp điểm 1.880 đồng/kWh và giờ cao điểm lên tới 5.313 đồng/kWh.
Mức giá trên chưa bao gồm thuế giá trị gia tăng.
| Khung giờ | Cấp điện áp từ trung áp trở lên | Cấp điện áp hạ áp đến 1 kV | 
|---|---|---|
| Bình thường | 2.829 | 3.089 | 
| Thấp điểm | 1.577 | 1.880 | 
| Cao điểm | 4.924 | 5.313 | 
Đáng chú ý, với khách hàng sử dụng điện ở cấp trung áp trở lên, giá giờ cao điểm là 4.924 đồng/kWh, cao gấp khoảng 3,12 lần mức 1.577 đồng/kWh vào giờ thấp điểm. Chênh lệch giữa hai khung giờ lên tới 3.347 đồng/kWh, tương đương 212,4%.
Trong khi đó, ở cấp điện áp hạ áp đến 1 kV, giá điện giờ cao điểm lên tới 5.313 đồng/kWh, cao gấp khoảng 2,83 lần mức 1.880 đồng/kWh vào giờ thấp điểm. Mức chênh lệch là 3.433 đồng/kWh.
Trước đó, tại Quyết định số 963 của Bộ Công Thương ban hành ngày 22/4/2026 quy định:
Giờ cao điểm: Từ thứ Hai đến thứ Bảy: từ 17h30 đến 22h30 (5 giờ/ngày); Chủ nhật không có giờ cao điểm.
Giờ bình thường: Từ thứ Hai đến thứ Bảy: từ 6h đến 17h30 và từ 22h30 đến 24h (13 giờ/ngày); Chủ nhật từ 06h00 đến 24h00 (18 giờ/ngày).

articles.title: Zipline nearly triples its value to $21.5bn as Walmart adds 300 sites
articles.text:
Zipline has raised $1.5bn at a $21.5bn valuation, the drone delivery company announced on Thursday. Paradigm, WCM Investment Management and Layer Global led the round. Valor Equity Partners, Fidelity, Uber, Tiger Global, J.P. Morgan, ARK Invest and Salesforce Ventures also invested.
On the same day, Walmart agreed to add 300 Zipline drone delivery sites in the US under a new multi-year deal. The two companies run 21 sites in Texas and Arkansas today, Bloomberg reported.
The valuation is almost three times the one Zipline reached in January, when it raised more than $600m. Bloomberg and Reuters put that earlier figure at $7.6bn, while The Wall Street Journal put it at $7.85bn.
Founder and chief executive Keller Cliffton told Bloomberg Television that demand had surprised both companies.
“I think both we and they have been quite startled by the level of customer demand.” Keller Cliffton, founder and CEO, Zipline
Where the money goes
Zipline said it will use the money to expand its US manufacturing and hire more staff as it builds a nationwide drone delivery network. Its factory near San Francisco International Airport can make up to 20,000 aircraft a year, according to Bloomberg.
Uber, which partnered with Zipline in August, is targeting 1m drone deliveries a day with the company by 2029, Zipline said. Zipline made more than 1m deliveries in the Dallas-Fort Worth area this year. Its median order in October arrived 19 minutes after checkout, against 30 minutes or more for ground delivery, the company said.
A group of its longest-standing restaurant partners saw delivery sales rise 26% between March and October. Zipline orders made up 80% of that increase, according to the company.
From medical supplies to takeaways
Cliffton co-founded Zipline in 2014. It began by flying blood to hospitals in Rwanda. Its African business now generates positive cash flow, Cliffton told Bloomberg. The company says it has flown 150m commercial autonomous miles without a safety incident.
It runs two drones. A long-range aircraft drops packages by parachute, and a quieter short-range drone lowers home deliveries on a tether. In the US, Zipline flies in Texas, Arkansas and Ohio. It plans to launch in Arizona soon, Kelly Cloonan reported for The Wall Street Journal.
Cliffton told the Journal that the national build-out would be hard.
“We have experience doing that, but still, this is a different scale and it’s going to be hard.” Keller Cliffton, Zipline
Rivals and hurdles
Regulatory approvals and community concerns over noise and safety still stand in the way of wider drone delivery, Reuters reported. Walmart also works with Alphabet’s Wing. Amazon is growing its drone service to about 500 US locations. DoorDash is building its own drones, and Ireland’s Manna is building a US factory.

articles.title: Instagram brings Edits to desktop to take on CapCut | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Instagram announced on Thursday that it’s bringing Edits, its short-form video editing app, to desktop on Mac. The desktop version is designed for more complex video-editing projects that benefit from a larger screen, mouse, and keyboard, the company says.
The move puts Edits in more direct competition with ByteDance’s CapCut, the video-editing app Meta sought to challenge when it launched Edits last year. CapCut, which is a massively popular tool for creators, has been available on desktop for Windows and Mac since 2021.
Instagram notes that the desktop app includes licensed and royalty-free music, sound and video effects, and automatic captions in multiple languages. Audio and text styles that creators saved on the mobile app sync over to the desktop app, and users can customize keyboard shortcuts or import them from other editing software.
It also features a full multi-track timeline, keyframes for transitions, audio waveforms for accurate cuts, and more. Additionally, creators can import their own font files.
“A lot of creators have described the same moment to us: a project gets too big for your phone,” Brett Westervelt, head of Edits, said in a blog post. “You’ve got a dozen clips going, you’re trying to land a cut on the exact beat, and your thumb covers the part of the timeline you need to see. Your work is growing, and your tools should grow with it. We’re expanding Edits to take on your most ambitious projects on desktop.”
Creators can publish from the desktop editor directly to Instagram with native features like tagging and location built in. The company says this gets rid of the need for creators to edit on desktop, download the file, move it to mobile, and then make more edits before posting it.
Edits will also support horizontal and vertical video formats, with watermark-free exports in 4K resolution for sharing across platforms or personal use, Instagram says.
The company plans to ship weekly updates to improve the desktop editor, noting that it’s currently working to make it possible for creators to edit one project across both desktop and mobile seamlessly.
Instagram also said it’s going to continue to grow the mobile Edits app for the more than 50 million creators who use it.

articles.title: Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 is $300 off ahead of Black Friday
articles.text:
Android fans with a bit of iPhone Duo envy, take note: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is discounted to $1,599.99 at both Amazon and Best Buy, a hefty $300 markdown from its usual price, and just $50 higher than the lowest we’ve seen. Considering the device only launched a few months ago, you’re saving a significant amount of cash on the unlocked device, and you can also opt for the 512GB model, doubling the storage, for just $200 more (Amazon, Best Buy). Best Buy currently has all three colors in stock, while the 256GB model is currently sold out on Amazon in cream.
Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 is $300 off ahead of Black Friday
You can also save on the Beats Pill Bluetooth speaker, a battery-powered Ring doorbell, and a Lego Star Wars droid.
The shorter and wider passport-style shape (similar to the iPhone Duo) quickly became natural and comfortable to handle, according to our reviewer Dominic Preston’s experience with the Z Fold 8. Despite its thin and light construction, it doesn’t skimp on battery life, with a 4,800mAh battery that still had 40 percent charge remaining after a full day of use. The interior 4:3 screen has the same ratio as most Apple iPads, which is great for watching movies or TV, but even better for reading. There’s no telephoto lens on this model (it’s present on the pricier Z Fold 8 Ultra), and it only has an IP48 rating, so you’ll want to be careful near the beach, but those are small compromises to make given the discounted price.
Other deals to consider
- Both Amazon and Best Buy are selling the Beats Pill for a discounted $99.95 and $99.99 respectively, a sizable break from the usual $149.99 price point. The 2024 edition of this iconic Bluetooth speaker adds in lossless audio over USB-C, as well as native feature support for both iOS and Android devices. It’s rated IP67 for dust and water resistance, and comes in three different colors to match your other Beats devices. Read our review.
- The Ring Battery Doorbell 2K is on sale for $39.99 at Amazon, over half off its $99.99 list price. This battery-powered doorbell camera is easy to install, and shoots clear 2K resolution video with a 140-degree field of view and up to 6X digital zoom. You’ll get real-time notifications on your phone for any activity the camera spots, with live view and two-way talk in case you need to have a chat with your neighbors or delivery folks without coming to the front door.
- You can pick up the Lego Star Wars: Ahsoka Chopper set for just $66.99 at Amazon, the lowest price we’ve seen yet for this 1,039-piece building kit. This brick-based droid has great play features, like detachable arms and center wheel for different display positions, and a head that spins and bobs realistically. It stands at over 8.5 inches when fully built, making it a fun addition to your existing Lego display or bookshelf.

articles.title: Guardian hands 1 million dental calls a year to Sierra's AI agents
articles.text:
Guardian Life signed a multi-year deal with Sierra to use its AI agents for about 1 million dental benefit verification calls a year, plus payments and claim status checks. It is Guardian’s third AI partnership in a year, after HCLTech and Avantos.
US insurer Guardian Life is handing some of its busiest customer service work to AI agents from Sierra, the startup run by former Salesforce co-chief executive Bret Taylor. The two signed a multi-year partnership, Guardian said on Thursday.
Guardian will use Sierra for about 1 million calls a year to check dental benefits, plus payments and questions about claim status. It says the aim is faster answers, but it has not shared any targets or financial terms. Sierra has argued that AI agents should be paid per result, not per seat.
“No one should have to sit on hold to check on a claim or confirm dental benefits,” said Taylor, Sierra’s chief executive and co-founder.
Michael Prestileo, Guardian’s chief strategy officer, said the deal would let staff focus on the cases where “human judgment and connection matter most.”
It is Guardian’s third AI deal in a year. In July, it signed a seven-year deal with HCLTech, which is taking over Guardian’s India centre and nearly 2,000 of its staff. In February, it invested in Avantos, an AI platform for financial advisers.
Sierra, launched in February 2024, says it works with 46% of the Fortune 50. It raised $950M at a $15B valuation in May. Rivals are consolidating: Salesforce, which Taylor once co-ran, is buying Fin for $3.6B.
It has been adding features fast. Last month, it teamed up with Stripe so its agents can take card payments during calls, and with Meta on an open standard for personal AI agents.

articles.title: ElevenLabs now lets users publish AI-generated music directly on SoundCloud | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Audio AI company ElevenLabs on Thursday said users will be able to publish AI-generated music created using its ElevenMusic platform directly on SoundCloud.
ElevenLabs is also offering SoundCloud Artist Pro users three months of ElevenMusic Pro, which lets you generate up to 1,000 songs, split songs’ stem files 500 times, and five custom styles or vocals per month.
The company first released a music-generation model in 2025, and followed it up in April 2026 with a consumer app that lets you generate songs using prompts. Then a month later, it released a new music model that could switch genres mid-track and handle more complex vocals. ElevenLabs said that users have so far created over 25 million tracks using its models.
SoundCloud has also been giving AI tools to artists, though it’s taking a different approach. Last month, it partnered with AI music tooling company Moises to let artists export and import songs to and from SoundCloud. The company also has integrations with other platforms like Google Flow Music and the music remix platform, Hook.
“SoundCloud has always been a place where artists experiment, push boundaries, and turn creative ideas into something bigger. By becoming the first platform to bring ElevenMusic creations directly to fans beyond its own ecosystem, we’re opening up new possibilities for artists to experiment, share their work, and build an audience,” SoundCloud CEO Eliah Seton said in a statement.
ElevenLabs also has a partnership with Spotify in which authors can use its audio models to generate narrations for their audiobooks and publish them on the music streaming service. While Spotify has signed partnerships with labels for products that let people use AI for remixing tracks, it has not yet announced any model partners like ElevenLabs.
Overall, though, music streaming platforms today seem more inclined toward labeling and helping users filter out AI-generated music, especially as the tech slowly grows popular with musicians. Deezer, for example, is introducing a toggle that lets you filter out AI music completely, while Bandcamp has put a blanket ban on AI-generated tracks. Spotify and YouTube have taken a more cautious approach to labeling tracks.

articles.title: Muse has a voice mode now
articles.text:
Meta now lets you have voice conversations with your Muse AI agent in real time, CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced today.
Muse has a voice mode now
Muse AI agent now has voices and ‘expressive’ avatars that animate while chatting with you.
The feature has been rolled out to me, and I gave it a spin on the iOS app while writing this article. As you chat with your Muse agent, the avatar at the top of your conversation animates in time with the words that it’s saying. You can also change the tone of the voice by just asking your agent about what you want and letting it decide or by browsing through a bunch of options in the avatar settings.
In my brief tests, my Muse agent responds quickly over voice, though it occasionally pauses while it’s looking up information or checking something for me (like it would with a text chat query). It also animates what it’s saying well, though for my particular avatar, it’s been a little uncanny. I set my Muse agent’s avatar to look like Mark Zuckerberg as a constant reminder that I’m chatting with a Meta service (I refuse to be charmed by a Jolly!), and seeing the digital Zuckerberg facsimile actually talk with me is quite weird. I also can’t get my Muse agent’s voice to sound exactly like Mark Zuckerberg.
Muse’s voice mode and expressive avatars are rolling out now in the US for the app, Meta says. They’re coming “soon” for Meta’s AI glasses and will also be available for its forthcoming Muse Charm gadget, which is supposed to ship this year.

articles.title: Nasdaq sell-off batters Asian chip stocks as SK Hynix, Samsung, Softbank, TSMC tumble
articles.text:
Asian technology stocks tumbled Friday, tracking a sharp sell-off on Wall Street overnight that sent the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite into correction territory as renewed concerns over artificial intelligence spending rattled investor sentiment.
South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix plunged over 8%, while Samsung Electronics shed 7%. LG Innotek and LG Display fell 10% and 7.7%, respectively, as selling pressure spread across the country's technology sector.
The rout came as investors worried that Democrats' sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections could lead to tighter restrictions on data-center development, potentially slowing demand for AI chips and related infrastructure.
In Japan, semiconductor-related stocks also fell, with chip-testing equipment maker Advantest plunging 12.2%, while Tokyo Electron slid 7.3%. Technology investment giant SoftBank Group tumbled 11.6%.
Shares of memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings fell nearly 10%, while Renesas Electronics declined 7.5%.
In Taiwan, semiconductor stocks also came under heavy selling pressure, with contract chipmaker TSMC sliding 9.6%. Electronics manufacturers Hon Hai Precision Industry, also known as Foxconn, and Foxconn Technology fell 9.4% and 9.1%, respectively, as the regional technology rout deepened.
The declines followed a brutal session on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq Composite sank 5.5%, amid mounting concerns over the sustainability of the AI investment boom and returns on massive data-center spending. It closed more than 10% below its recent peak. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12.2%.
The sell-off in Asian equities has been exacerbated by investors unwinding positions, stop-loss selling and heightened volatility, Timothy Moe, chief Asia Pacific equity strategist at Goldman Sachs, told CNBC's "Squawk Box Asia" on Friday.
He added that potential political opposition to U.S. data center construction may affect demand and profits for Asian AI hardware suppliers.
"If there's concern about the speed and magnitude of buildout in the U.S., then obviously that's going to put all that into question," he said. "The market's tendency is always to shoot first and ask questions later. I think that's exactly what's happening now."

articles.title: Costco is taking aim at its May record high — how it got here and where's it going
articles.text: Costco is finally back. The warehouse retailer stock was one of just three Club names in the green in Thursday's ugly market. (Fellow defensive names Cardinal Health and Kimberly-Clark were the other two). While off session highs, Costco's nearly 2% advance put it ever closer to its May record high of $1,094 — a far cry from just a couple of months ago when it appeared stuck below $900. But since bottoming out in mid-September, shares are up more than 19%. The rally in Costco has been driven by two things. First, there has been a rotation into safer stocks and away from the AI trade. While Thursday's obliteration of Wall Street's postelection rally was the most severe example, this has been going on to a lesser extent for weeks. Will it last? Who knows, based on the past two days in the market. The second thing going for Costco is strong company fundamentals — the latest being October sales. It's that second point — one that is far more within management's control — that we want to dig into. For October, Costco reported net sales of $24.5 billion, a 12.6% increase from a year earlier, with comparable sales up 11.1%. Excluding gas sales and currency fluctuations, comps rose a better-than-expected 7.3%, according to Goldman Sachs analysts. When asked earlier on "Squawk on the Street" whether Costco shares could surpass its May record, Jim confidently responded, "Yeah, we will." While the stock has been steadily rising since Sept. 16, the rally really kicked into high gear about a week later after the company reported solid fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter earnings and progress addressing slowing membership growth rates and wobbly renewal trends. "Costco is a volume store. It's not a price store," Jim said, pointing to the retailer's use of competitive pricing to attract large numbers of customers while also generating a windfall from membership fees. "I continue to think that Costco represents great value." Costco's gasoline business is a prime example at a time when fuel prices have been soaring due to the Iran war-driven higher cost of oil. During September's earnings call, CEO Ron Vachris said that gas had a record year. "During the fiscal year, we estimate we saved our members over $3.2 billion versus the average price at the pump in markets where we operate," Vachris said. "We also expanded 26 existing U.S. gas stations during this year at our highest volume locations to increase throughput and improve the overall member experience." While gas is not terribly profitable, it's been key to getting more traffic into the stores because consumers heading to the pump for Costco's below-retail-priced fuel are also apt to swing inside to shop. COST YTD mountain Costco YTD The stock, however, is not cheap at nearly 47 times fiscal 2027 earnings estimates. It never has been. Jim talked about how the late Charlie Munger's views on Costco's lofty price-to-earnings valuation have shaped his. "Munger said this is the only stock in his whole lexicon that he felt you have to not pay that much attention to the P/E," Jim said. "I've adopted that for a long time." Munger, who was Warren Buffett's longtime right-hand man at Berkshire Hathaway, served on Costco's board. Munger was willing to look past the stock's premium multiple and own the stock for the long term because he believed so strongly in its business model, moat, and customer loyalty. We share that admiration, which is why we've owned Costco stock for years. But we also recognize that a high valuation means there's little room for error when the company has operational hiccups. The numbers need to be near-perfect or else its sainted status could be in question. That's why the decline in membership renewal rates stretching back to last year was so worrisome for us. But it is also why shares have reacted favorably since its fiscal Q4 earnings report showed a sequential improvement in worldwide renewal rates. (Jim Cramer's Charitable Trust is long COST. articles.title: Jim Cramer explains why no AI stock seems safe from the market carnage
articles.text:
CNBC's Jim Cramer said Thursday that uncertainty over the future of a data center build-out has made artificial intelligence stocks increasingly difficult to value, leading to the steep selling over the past two sessions.
The sell-off swept across the AI trade, hitting everything from chipmakers to companies supplying power and electrical equipment for data centers. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) fell 3% Wednesday and another 10% Thursday, while GE Vernova and Sandisk dropped 7% and 22%, respectively, on Thursday. Investors are concerned that regulatory hurdles and opposition to new data centers could slow the build-out, undermining the growth forecasts supporting chipmakers' valuations.
"We don't know what to pay for any of the stocks connected to the data center and that's why this moment is so fraught," the "Mad Money" host said.
Cramer pointed to Nvidia as a prime example. The AI chipmaker trades at roughly 12 times next year's earnings with an expected growth rate of 70%, making it appear remarkably cheap. But those earnings projections assume demand will remain strong for years to come.
"That's an incredible bargain," he said. "But it is not a bargain if, the following year, it can't grow any further, because the U.S. won't permit new data centers as fast as they do now."
Memory maker Micron also faces risk. The company's long-term take-or-pay contracts provide some revenue visibility even if customers don't take delivery of their chips. However, Cramer said he's unsure how sturdy those contracts would be if any signees fell on especially hard times and didn't have the money to pay.
Advanced Micro Devices presents another valuation dilemma. Cramer praised its latest earnings as "one of the best quarters I have ever seen" and highlighted CEO Lisa Su's projection that the broader data center market could eventually reach $1 trillion.
"If that's the case then you can buy her [CEO Lisa Su's] stock right now," Cramer said. "Do you want to? The stock was at $188 in March. By that token, $404 seems awfully high to me. Maybe that's the real problem."
Ultimately, Cramer said the question is whether regulatory hurdles will significantly slow data center construction or merely delay it. Until the outlook becomes clearer, even exceptional earnings outlook may not be enough to justify AI stocks' valuations.

articles.title: Jim Cramer says the AI sell-off isn't over, but it isn't another dot-com crash
articles.text:
The steep sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks likely has further to go, CNBC's Jim Cramer predicted Thursday — but he urged investors not to panic.
Growing opposition to new data centers following the midterm elections has raised doubts about future AI infrastructure spending, sending shares of companies tied to the buildout sharply lower. Micron tumbled 17%, GE Vernova dropped 7% and Sandisk plunged 22% on Thursday. All three stocks were also crushed in Wednesday's session.
"I wish I could say that today's flush was the bottom," the "Mad Money" host said, before cautioning that there may be more downside ahead, though he didn't believe this was an internet bubble redux. Cramer argued that today's AI companies are fundamentally different from the speculative businesses that collapsed during the dot-com bust.
"But I look at the charts, and there still seems like there's no support for so many Tech stocks, especially the semis, because they ran so much on the way up. However it might feel, it's actually an orderly decline because unlike 2000, these are mostly lucrative companies with stocks that went too high."
Investors had pushed AI stocks too high by assuming the rapid pace of data center construction would continue indefinitely, Cramer said. Smaller developers such as CoreWeave, Iren and Nebius face particular risks because they borrowed money to finance projects that could now face regulatory delays.
"That's what I am chiefly worried about," he said. "That's the real problem. That's what could really hurt the stock market. ... Right now, no one of significance is defaulting on their debt. The only issue with the debt is that it's connected to those neocloud companies that I mentioned. That's not enough to sink us."
Cramer suggested that a swift sell-off could help the market work off the excesses of the AI boom more effectively than a prolonged downturn.
"I for one am glad they are ripping the Band-Aid off this market rather than slowing trying to take it off a little bit each day," he said.
For investors, Cramer recommended maintaining sufficient cash. While semiconductor stocks could face further declines, he pointed to falling interest rates, signs of easing inflation and the possibility of an end to the Iran war as reasons for optimism.
"If you have cash you won't panic," Cramer concluded. "You won't be complacent, either. You will be clear-headed and that's how you will lose less money until things get better. They always do."

articles.title: Stock futures fall after Nasdaq correction; Japan's Nikkei 225 enters bear market: Live updates
articles.text:
Stock futures fell Thursday evening after a punishing sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks that sent the Nasdaq into correction territory. Traders also awaited a key payrolls report.
S&P 500 futures lost 0.6%, while Nasdaq-100 futures slid 0.8%. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average shed 291 points, or 0.6%.
In Asia, South Korea led losses in the region, with the Kospi plunging more than 8% to slip below the 5,000 mark. Japan's Nikkei 225 dropped more than 6%, falling into bear market territory. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 slipped 0.9%.
The moves follow a bout of heavy selling during Thursday's regular Wall Street session that saw the three major averages post their worst one-day performances since April 2025. The Nasdaq Composite tanked 5.5%, closing more than 10% below its most recent high and landing in correction territory. The broad-market S&P 500 lost 4.4%, while the Dow fell more than 1,800 points, or 3.4%.
While all 11 sectors of the S&P 500 closed with losses, shares of companies tied to the AI build-out suffered keenly. Democrats' big wins in the House and Senate, as well as key governorships in states like Texas, sparked traders' worries of a potential slowdown in data center construction.
Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices plummeted 17% each, while neocloud CoreWeave slid 10%. Even the Magnificent Seven weren't spared, as Nvidia dropped 9%, turning negative for 2026, and the cohort of tech juggernauts shed more than $1 trillion in aggregate market cap.
The three major averages are poised for losses on the week, with the Nasdaq down 4.4% and the S&P 500 off almost 3% in the period. The 30-stock Dow is the relative outperformer of the three, off just 0.5% week to date.
The pullback creates a buying opportunity, Victoria Greene, CIO at G Squared Private Wealth told CNBC Thursday. "The AI trade, in my opinion, is not dead here," she said, adding, "it's a good discount." She's interested in memory stocks, citing how management teams throughout this earnings season have been talking about the capacity crunch. "Buying a volatile dip tends to be good as long as we're still in a non-recessionary period," she said.
Another market catalyst awaits investors on Friday morning in the form of the October payrolls report. The Dow Jones consensus estimate is for 59,000 jobs added last month and for the unemployment rate to hold steady at 4.2%.
Correction: Victoria Greene is the CIO of G Squared Private Wealth. An earlier version misspelled her name.

articles.title: Mississippi Senate election: Democrat Scott Colom narrowly leads Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith
articles.text:
Mississippi's uncalled Senate election could provide one of the biggest shocks in a midterm election cycle already chock full of stunning defeats of Republican candidates.
Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, the GOP incumbent, is trailing Democratic nominee Scott Colom in an extraordinarily tight race in normally solidly red Mississippi. Colom had 49.04% of the counted ballots, compared to 48.85% for Hyde-Smith, with an estimated more than 95% of the votes in, according to the Associated Press.
Colom's ultra-thin lead ticked up slightly late Thursday afternoon to 1,813 votes out of a total of 951,744 counted as of 6:17 p.m. ET, the AP said. Ty Pinkins, an independent candidate, had 20,007 votes, or 2.1% of the total count.
A final result may not be available until next week because more ballots can still arrive and be counted.
Mississippi's election procedures do not have an automatic recount provision.
"Absolutely, I didn't think it would be this close," said Brian Anderson, a political science professor at the Mississippi University for Women in Columbus.
Anderson said that before the election, he thought Colom, a 43-year-old district attorney, might get into position to lose by just 3 or 4 percentage points, which would have been a very solid showing in a state that hasn't elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1982.
"I'm much more surprised" now that Colom has a chance to win, Anderson said.
If Colom defeats Hyde-Smith, 67, he would be the first Black senator from Mississippi since the post-Civil War Reconstruction Era.
"The Democrats have struggled here to create a pipeline of candidates," Anderson said. A Colom win "would galvanize the Democratic Party in a way it has not been," he said.
Neither candidate's campaign immediately responded to requests for comment from CNBC.
Hyde-Smith's X account, in a post Thursday afternoon, said, "Cindy Hyde-Smith is going to represent Mississippi in the United States Senate for the next six years."
"We believe thousands of votes remain to be counted from dozens of Republican counties, and we are confident those votes will reinforce her path to victory," the post said. "Election officials are continuing the normal process of counting outstanding ballots, including absentee ballots. They must have the time to complete that work and ensure every lawful ballot is accurately counted and every Mississippian's voice is heard."
The post added, "We expect Democratic lawyers to pull out every stop, and we are prepared. Our focus is on completing the count and returning Cindy Hyde-Smith to the Senate to keep fighting for Mississippi values."
Also on Thursday, the Republican National Committee sent a text message blast to subscribers, asking for donations of $25 by citing the hyper-close race in Mississippi and saying Hyde-Smith needed support for monitoring ballot reviews.
"Mississippi is the firewall, and this race is our line in the sand," the message said.
In a pair of ironic twists, if Colom wins, his victory could be attributed in some ways to actions taken by two Republicans: President Donald Trump and Hyde-Smith herself.
Supreme Court Justice Amy Coney Barrett, whom Trump appointed, wrote the court's 5-4 majority ruling in June that upheld a Mississippi law allowing mail-in absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day to be counted if they are received within five business days.
Those ballots could provide Colom a margin of victory. There are also an estimated 10,000 to 15,000 provisional ballots that require verification of eligibility to vote.
A lawyer for the Republican National Committee, whose lawsuit argued federal law barred counting votes received after Election Day, noted in a brief to the Supreme Court, "Democratic voters tend to mail their ballots later on average than Republican voters, which results in late-arriving ballots favoring Democratic candidates."
Trump at the time of the Supreme Court ruling called it "a tremendous loss" for voters' rights.
Hyde-Smith was appointed to her Senate seat in 2018 after the resignation of Thad Cochran and later that year won a special election for the seat. She was elected to a full term in 2020.
In 2023, she effectively blocked Colom's nomination by then-President Joe Biden to a post as a federal judge for the Northern District of Mississippi. Colom's nomination had the support of Mississippi's other Republican senator, Roger Wicker, and two former GOP governors.
Hyde-Smith said she opposed Colom's nomination for reasons that included his purported support for transgender students participating in girls' sports and because his campaign for district attorney had allegedly received money from billionaire George Soros.
Colom, in an April 10, 2023, letter to Hyde-Smith, said he was unaware before his hometown newspaper reported it that Soros had donated to a political action committee that had supported his campaign. He also wrote that he was not sure why Hyde-Smith had suggested he "opposed legislation to protect female athletes."
Colom concluded the letter by promising to be guided by the law, not his personal views on public policy, if he were confirmed as a judge.
"I hope you will reconsider your views about my nomination," he wrote.
Hyde-Smith did not reconsider her views and maintained her block on the nomination.
Colom announced his candidacy for the Democratic nomination for Senate in September 2025 and recently told CNN, "Me not having a federal judgeship is not a motivating factor for me at all" in running.
Anderson said Hyde-Smith ran "a low-visibility campaign," at least compared to Colom's, and that she focused on voters who traditionally would be expected to support her.
Hyde-Smith refused to debate Colom several times.
Colom "knows how to speak to people's interests, and Hyde-Smith was all about values, which is great for a lot of people, but it's all about the interests right now," Anderson said.
Those interests include concerns about affordability, the Iran war and corruption.
Colom is "bringing up all those," Anderson said.
Anderson noted that Colom's campaign had pounced on a remark Hyde-Smith made during a Feb. 22 interview with a local television outlet.
In the interview, Hyde-Smith answered a question about rising beef prices by saying, "You know, there so many proteins to choose from."
Colom's campaign featured a video clip of that remark in an ad featuring people reacting incredulously to Hyde-Smith's suggestion.
"Pick another protein?" one woman said in the ad. "She done lost her d--- mind. I'd rather pick another senator."

articles.title: Neocloud IREN says $4 billion in annualized revenue being delayed due to customer request
articles.text:
Following a 26% post-election plunge in its stock price, neocloud IREN said in its earnings report on Thursday that over $4 billion in annual recurring revenue projected to land in 2026 has been pushed out to at least January.
IREN said the move, which could extend payment to February, is due to "a customer-requested change and supplier timing."
On the company's earnings call, IREN co-CEO Daniel Roberts said Microsoft is the customer.
"They made a request to reconfigure and upgrade some of the network infrastructure and the purpose of that was really to enable the 200 megawatts of capacity to service these latest-generation frontier models," Roberts said.
Shares of IREN rose in extended trading, but that comes after a 55% drop over the past month.
The company said revenue climbed 66% from the prior quarter to $228 million, beating the $221 million average analyst estimate, according to LSEG. AI Cloud revenue more than doubled to $200 million. IREN gets the rest of its revenue from bitcoin mining, which was its primary business before the company pivoted to AI.
IREN's net loss narrowed to $263 million from $684 million the prior period. Year-ago figures weren't included in the earnings release.
The company is being closely watched by investors as the AI trade shows signs of unwinding, particularly following the Democratic sweep in Tuesday's midterm elections. Concerns are mounting that cash-burning companies reliant on debt are going to have a hard time meeting their obligations as interest rates rise and lenders back out of the market. The Nasdaq had its worst day on Thursday since April 2025.
"Capital markets have become more selective in the last few weeks, and the questions have undoubtedly moved from how big the contract is to whether it can be delivered, financed, and run at a profit," Roberts said on the call.
CoreWeave, which is set to report earnings on Tuesday, has plunged 60% in the past month. Nebius, which reports next Thursday, is down 48% over that stretch.
IREN said revenue backlog increased 22% from the prior period to $20.3 billion, with "approximately two-thirds with investment-grade counterparties." The $4 billion ARR target is fully contracted and funded, the company said.
"There is a disconnect between what we're seeing in public market and what we're seeing at the customer level," Roberts told CNBC's Seema Mody.
Still, Iren said it planed to shell out $15 billion in capital expenditures the rest of this fiscal year, including $9 billion in cash and committed financing, and $6 billion in "target" financing, which is "subject to market conditions."
The neocloud said that prices for its compute continue to rise and that it expanded an existing contract with a leading frontier AI lab. It said it has contracts with Nvidia, Microsoft and 13 other customers.
Roberts said that some data center construction in the coming year would be backed by Nvidia and Microsoft, but about a third would be to companies that are willing to offer large prepayments for the capacity.
"We just had a customer agree to fund 90% of the GPU capex," Roberts said, referring to graphics processing units.
IREN said that community opposition can be addressed by tapping local suppliers, using water efficiently and creating jobs.
"I think whether it's Texas, whether it's Australia, whether it's Spain, everywhere, all we're seeing is people wanting to ensure that data centers pay their own way and do the right thing, and it it feels completely reasonable," Roberts said.
IREN said it deliberately hadn't yet bought all of the GPUs it needs for next year to reduce risk.
—CNBC's Isabel O'Brien contributed to this report.
